prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the driver in a rear-end collision in Pasadena, Texas, and has neck and back strain. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1055; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Thank you for taking the time to speak with me today. This recorded statement concerns the collision you were involved in on the Pasadena, Texas roadway. Can you confirm that you are comfortable continuing?

A: Yes, I'm comfortable. Go ahead.

Q: Please describe what you were doing right before the impact.

A: I was stopped at a traffic light in the right lane. The light was red, and I had been waiting for maybe fifteen or twenty seconds when I felt the hit from behind.

Q: Were you wearing your seatbelt at the time?

A: Yes, I was.

Q: How fast would you estimate the other vehicle was traveling when it struck you?

A: I didn't see it coming, so I can't say for sure. It felt like a hard hit, though. My head snapped back and then forward.

Q: Did your vehicle move after the impact?

A: Yes, it lurched forward into the car in front of me. I don't think I hit it hard, but my car did move.

Q: Did you feel any injuries immediately after the collision?

A: Not right away. About an hour later my neck started to ache, and by the next morning I had stiffness and pain across my lower back too.

Q: Have you sought medical treatment since the collision?

A: Yes, I saw my doctor and I've been doing physical therapy twice a week. The doctor diagnosed me with neck and back strain.

Q: Are you currently experiencing any limitations in your daily activities?

A: Yes, it's hard to lift anything heavy, and I've had trouble sleeping because of the pain. I've also missed some work.

Q: Is there anything else you would like to add to your statement?

A: No, I think that covers it. I just hope this gets resolved soon.

Q: Thank you. This concludes the recorded statement.
